title: Assemble the diagonal orientation in ordered tower coordinates
statement: Fix a finite field datum $D$ of characteristic $p$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and Noetherian separated finite-type schemes $X,Y$ over the fixed algebraic closure. Let $f:X\to Y$ be smooth of relative dimension $d\ge0$, with a factorization $X\xrightarrow{j}Z\xrightarrow{p}Y$ in which $j$ is an open immersion and $p$ is proper. Use the strict coefficient towers, their uniform constructible finite-Tor categories, and fixed adjunction/evaluation presentations [det-sp-tower-gluing, sk-def-sp-normalized-towers]. There exist normalized coefficient-unit, root, K-flat tensor and pullback presentations [def-sp-tower-gamma-data], and an isomorphism from the ordered $d$-fold shifted Tate line to the given exceptional image of the coefficient unit. At every positive level its evaluation is the inverse finite diagonal orientation, including the exact scalar-unit equation and prescribed WordComparison square. No tensor-transpose isomorphy or naturality, and no normalized-output assertion, is included.

source.place: (1), finite diagonal orientations and strict-heart assembly

proof.text:
identify the ell-power quotients with the uniformizer quotients using the
ramification equation in b. Take the normalized scalar-unit, root, K-flat tensor
and pullback comparisons, which fix their maps on sections and representatives.
The finite diagonal theorem supplies the inverse orientations at every positive
level. FiniteOrientationReduction identifies their quotient squares with the
actual reductions of the given right adjoint at the coefficient unit. Remove the
common shift 2d. Scalar extension of the locally free Tate line is its ordinary
quotient, so StrictLineHeartAssembly assembles the compatible degree-zero sheaf
maps, and their inverses, into a strict tower isomorphism. Shift back and use the
ordered tensor/shift reassociation to obtain orientation. Its prescribed evaluation
is exactly DiagonalLevels, including the coefficient-unit equation. The zero-fold
line uses the coefficient unit, so the construction also applies at d=0.
